thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on /v1/streaming/generate (us-west1). p99=3.8s (SLO=2.5s), p95=1.9s. Streaming stalls reported by multiple customers. Alert: https://ops.example.com/alerts/ALERT-1783001234 :rotating_light:

jordan (oncall-sre): I’m on it. Paging maya + prod-obs. brief plan: quick-impact check -> try scale/route -> short mitigation -> notify customers -> deeper triage.

maya (eng-runtime): ping. saw the p99 jump around 17:03 UTC. Grafana shows a spike in tail latency for streaming sessions with long seq lengths (>1024). Link: https://grafana.example.com/d/streaming/latency?orgId=1

lee (prod-obs): adding context: continuous batching queue depth for streaming workers climbed from 30 -> 420. There are backpressure retries in the logs correlated with slow KV-cache misses to redis-cache-3.

jordan (oncall-sre): ops checklist (quick):
1) confirm scope (customer count + routes)
2) check worker pod/gpu saturation
3) try temporary routing to fallback model-quantized variant
4) increase worker pool (scale up)
5) if streaming stalls persist, enable drop-to-sync-responses (disable streaming) for affected customers

sam (infra): running quick checks ->
```
# check node gpu/cpu
kubectl top pods -n runtime | grep runtime-worker
# check redis latency
redis-cli -h redis-cache-3 latency latest
```
sam (infra): redis latency shows 120ms p99 (baseline ~3ms). Worker GPU utilization is 78%, but CPU wait and RX queues look high on several pods.

maya (eng-runtime): two fast mitigations I can push now: 1) route new streaming requests from hostnames matching customer tier=free to model:llama-small-q8 (lower memory, faster tokens) 2) enable prefix-KV cache warmup for hot prefixes. Routing snippet: 
```
POST /routing/v1/policy/apply
{
  "match": "customer.tier == \"free\" && endpoint == \"/v1/streaming/generate\"",
  "route_to": "model://llama-small-q8@us-west1",
  "priority": 100
}
```
maya (eng-runtime): I can also flip on temporary non-streaming fallback for 2 high-impact customers if we need deterministic latencies.

jordan (oncall-sre): go for the routing change, maya. sam, please escalate redis pod to high-priority node pool and restart redis-cache-3. lee, can you confirm which customers are getting error/large retries? ana, please start customer impact messaging.

sam (infra): restarting redis-cache-3 now. logs: 
```
[2026-03-14T17:05:12Z] systemd: stopping redis-cache-3
[2026-03-14T17:05:18Z] systemd: redis-cache-3 started
```
sam (infra): post-restart p99 redis latency -> 5ms. Good.

maya (eng-runtime): routing change applied at 17:07 UTC. Will monitor.

lee (prod-obs): after routing + redis restart: queue depth dropped to ~60, p95=1.1s, p99=2.3s. Still above SLO but trending down. No errors in streaming logs aside from a few enqueue retries.

ana (customer-success): (ana): quick status: looks like 3 paying customers saw degraded response times on a subset of calls (mostly long conversations). I’ve sent an initial DM to account owners and created a PSR. Customers asked for ETA and mitigation — they prefer fallback to non-stream if latency persists.

jordan (oncall-sre): temporary mitigation summary applied: routing to llama-small-q8 for free tier + redis restart. Observability still watching for stalls.

maya (eng-runtime): additional step: enable KV caching for the 2 hot prefixes. Patch rolling now (should be <90s).

ravi (next-oncall): I’m taking the handoff at 17:15 UTC for post-mitigation validation and RCA. Notes:
- current state: p95 back to ~1.0s, p99 ~1.9s; streaming stall count decreased by 88%
- outstanding: verify no regression in generation quality from model switch for free tier, follow-up on autoscaling thresholds for streaming workers, tune redis autoscaling policy

jordan (oncall-sre): marking incident as Mitigated (customer impact reduced) at 17:16 UTC. Will keep channel open for RCA.

lee (prod-obs): quick follow-ups for RCA:
- correlate long sequence sessions with prefix cache misses
- evaluate batching policy (we may need another knob to cap max batch latency for streaming)
- review routing fallback latency characteristics

ana (ana): customers updated with ETA ~1h for full remediation + explanation that we applied temporary routing and cache fixes.

jordan (oncall-sre): Post-incident action items (short):
- create a Grafana alert for streaming queue depth > 200 sustained for 5m (assigned: lee)
- tighten redis p99 alerting + autoscale (assigned: sam)
- add canary test for streaming fallback path (assigned: maya)
- customer postmortem + communication (assigned: ana)

ravi (next-oncall): taking ownership of the follow-ups. Handoff complete.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: ALARM-1783001234 -> mitigated at 1783001376 (metadata: severity=sev2, impacted_customers=3, mitigation_actions=[routing,fallback_cache_restart])

jordan (oncall-sre): closing thread for active ops. Will open postmortem doc and link here. Thx all :thumbsup:
